name: model-fit
description: Checks every prompt locally (zero tokens). When the current model is likely too weak or overkill, it blocks the prompt and shows a dialog ("Don't use X for this task"), recommending the model with the best predicted fit per cost.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Check every prompt and block with a dialog when the current model looks wrong for it. /model-fit on|off (or typing model-fit on|off) toggles it too.

minConfidence.title: Minimum confidence
minConfidence.description: How sure the local rules must be (0.5 to 0.95) before a mismatch blocks the prompt and opens a dialog. Fixed: dismissing dialogs never raises it.

askOnStandard.title: Also ask for ordinary tasks
askOnStandard.description: Off by default: an ordinary task (not light, not deep) on a borderline or roomy model only gets a status-line hint. On: those also block and open the dialog.

onDismiss.title: When the dialog is dismissed (Esc)
onDismiss.description: hold (default): the prompt is NOT sent; it is shown back so you can resend it and pick an option. send: the prompt is sent as typed.

minWords.title: Minimum words
minWords.description: Shorter prompts are ignored unless they match a strong rule.

useClassifier.title: Use a small model for unclear prompts
useClassifier.description: Off by default (no token cost). When on, a prompt the local rules cannot place is sent to the haiku model once to pick light, standard or deep.

statusLine.title: Status line
statusLine.description: Show a one-line, non-blocking verdict after each checked prompt, for example "model-fit: Opus fits" or "model-fit: overkill, Haiku would do (~5x cheaper)".

showButton.title: On/off button
showButton.description: Show a small ON/OFF button in the band above the prompt box (terminal and desktop) that turns model-fit on or off. It never replaces another band.

costRatios.title: Relative model costs
costRatios.description: A ROUGH ratio of list prices, comma separated, for example haiku=1,sonnet=3,opus=5 (fable=8 is optional). It goes stale when prices change: edit it. Used only to pick the cheapest model predicted to be good enough. Bad pieces are ignored.
